boardStatus: The institutional offering is a genuine physician fellowship, not a generic directory category, research-only postdoctoral appointment, or non-physician supplement. The public BWH/MGB page describes a two-year combined open and endovascular neurovascular surgery fellowship (Track B) for neurosurgery residency graduates with prior endovascular experience. CAST's current accredited-program directory lists Massachusetts General Brigham as a Neuroendovascular fellowship (NI1023, list updated December 2025); this listing is evidence of a CAST Neuroendovascular program at MGB, but the public record does not conclusively crosswalk the directory entry to every detail of BWH's combined Track B. ACGME separately recognizes Neuroendovascular Intervention as a 24-month subspecialty program; no public source retrieved in this review established that the specific BWH combined Track B is ACGME-accredited. The CNS Endovascular Recognition of Focused Practice Designation (RFPD) is an ABMS-approved joint focused-practice credential sponsored by ABNS, ABR, and ABPN, managed by ABNS, with a written exam; it is not a separate medical-specialty board certification. The applicable pathway depends on base-board certification and prerequisite training. No exam blueprint/domain weights were located in public sources; content mapping here is to published ACGME/CAST requirements and RFPD procedure categories, not a claim to reproduce or predict the exam.
boardEligibilityNotice: The BWH page states that its two-year offering is open to graduates of a seven-year ACGME-approved neurological surgery residency who have performed at least 200 catheter-based diagnostic and/or interventional cerebral angiographic procedures as primary operator. That institutional statement is not equivalent to ACGME/CAST accreditation status, ABNS board eligibility, or eligibility for the RFPD. ABNS base certification, current program rules, documented practice/cases, the appropriate credential pathway, and any future rule changes must be checked directly with the boards. ABR/ABPN pathways described on the joint RFPD page do not make those applicants eligible for the BWH Track B unless the institution confirms it. Do not use this curriculum to claim eligibility or credentials.

boardNames: American Board of Plastic Surgery (ABPS) — primary plastic-surgery certification only; no separate microsurgery or breast-reconstruction board exam identified in the checked public sources.
boardStatus: The official MGB offering is a clinical physician fellowship: applicants must have completed a plastic surgery residency, and the page describes sequential two-month apprenticeship blocks with a small number of attendings. The fellowship is not a generic directory label, combined residency, research-only job or non-physician supplement. MGB states that it participates in the San Francisco Match for Microsurgery. ABMS lists ABPS certification in Plastic Surgery and subspecialty certificates in Plastic Surgery Within the Head and Neck and Surgery of the Hand; no separate microsurgery or breast reconstruction certificate/exam is identified on the checked ABMS page. The current ACGME plastic-surgery overview lists Hand Surgery and Craniofacial Plastic Surgery as plastic surgery subspecialties, not microsurgery or breast reconstruction. A 2020 peer-reviewed review described no formal microsurgery certification then; that is a dated secondary source, not a current regulator. No fellowship-specific board exam was located as of the date checked.
boardEligibilityNotice: A plastic-surgery residency prerequisite does not establish ABPS exam eligibility. Candidates must independently confirm current requirements with ABPS and the programme/match. This course grants no ABPS eligibility, licensure, accredited training, institutional status or board certification and never guarantees passing.
